newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE 100 ends higher snaps losing streak.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE 100 ends higher snaps losing streak.

text.p: UK's blue chip share index snapped a six-day losing streak on Tuesday as bid speculation coupled with a solid rebound on Wall Street lifted sentiment, dealers said.
The benchmark FTSE 100 closed 20.5 points higher at 4,596.3, after shedding 207 points during the previous six sessions.
Yet, today's advance was not broad-based, with FTSE 100 advancers narrowly outpacing decliners 52 to 45.

"What we've got here is a relatively polarised performance," said BZW stock strategist Steve Wright. "It's mixed. The financials are up, but there are a lot of big decliners and concerns about valuations and growth."

The Dow, which registered its second largest point loss ever on Monday, was up about 46 points when London markets closed, as bargain hunters rushed in after Japan reassured investors that it did not intend to sell U.S. government bonds.
The FTSE 100 got off to a shaky start, falling as low as 4,538.3 initially, on the back of Monday's 132 points slide in the Dow.
Dealers and strategists played down the losses on Wall Street and called London's muted reaction to it encouraging.
"We've seen this sort of (sell-off) a hundred times and the last hundred times it has been a catalyst to new highs," said Nick Knight, global stock strategist with Nomura.
Dealers said recent losses in London had been overdone and that at least a small rebound was in order.
Nick Glydon, a technical analyst with Robert Fleming Securities, noted that the FTSE 100 has only had six straight losing sessions 14 times since the index was established in 1984.
"Every time that has happened, the market has been higher 45 days later and on average, 300 points higher three months later," Glydon said.
The market was led by the bank sector as bid speculation boiled over.
Shares in National Westminster Bank Plc, the best performing FTSE 100 stock, surged to a four-month high as bid talk reached fever pitch.
NatWest shares added 43p, or 5.5 percent, to 826-1/2p, on top of Monday's 37p advance after press reports said the bank could be a target for Barclays Plc.
Royal Bank of Scotland Plc was also at the centre of bid talk. Its shares jumped 15-1/2p to 598-1/2, after a press report said the group could be a target for HSBC Holdings Plc .
Among others in the sector, Lloyds TSB Group Plc advanced 20p to 629-1/2 in active trade. Shares in Standard Chartered Bank firmed 38p to 912.
"As soon as we see buyers in one stock in the sector, the market makers put the others up as well to compensate for the short positions," a dealer said.
In other trading, shares in Cable & Wireless Communications Plc and Telewest Communications Plc jumped after a press report said the two companies were in talks that could lead to a merger.
CWC shares finished 28-1/2p higher to 587-1/2, while TeleWest shares added 4-1/2p to 98-1/2.

The Times newspaper said the two groups were in talks to form a common television and 'phone brand that could lead to a merger, increasing their ability to compete with British Telecommunications Plc and British Sky Broadcasting Plc.
BSkyB shares were hit by another press report that said soccer clubs were considering setting up their own television service when their deal with Sky expires in 2001.
BSkyB shares, already down 19 percent since June 12 -- partly due to the company being told to exit a group bidding for a digital television licence -- lost another 18p to close at 468-1/2.
Shares in Granada Plc and Carlton Communications Plc firmed after their joint venture British Digital Broadcasting (BDB) was awarded a digital terrestrial broadcasting licence.
Shares in Carlton rose 9p to 525-1/2p, while Granada gained 19-1/2p to 845-1/2.
